public_rationale: Contemporaneous reporting described Chinese authorities considering limits on H200 purchases. That supports Marcus's qualified observation of some government reluctance. The same FT account said no final decision had been made and that major Chinese technology companies would welcome the chips. It does not support a blanket claim that China lacked demand or had already rejected H200 imports.
limitations: Support is for a qualified report about government reluctance.
The underlying discussions were attributed to unnamed sources.
Commercial demand and government permission are distinct.
The original FT page was inaccessible; an attributed reproduction was read.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: China appears, to some degree, not to want the Nvidia H200s it is now licensed to buy.

statement.excerpt: In unexpected news just reported by the FT (as summarized below), that seems in fact to be happening to some degree.
statement.document_title: Has the Chinese government figured out the fact that GPUs ≠ AGI?

from_speaker: news just reported by the FT
our_interpretation: The contextual referent is Chinese government reluctance to permit unrestricted H200 purchases, rather than an absence of demand among Chinese companies.
The qualified wording commits to a credible reported indication of reluctance. It does not assert that a final restriction had already been adopted.
The observation covers December 8–9, 2025. Later purchasing behavior cannot independently settle what was being reported at that time.
The references to degree and the FT qualify an observation; they are not antecedents of a conditional forecast.
criteria.support_condition: Credible contemporaneous reporting describes Chinese authorities considering or imposing limits on H200 purchases after the U.S. announcement.
criteria.contradiction_condition: The relevant report is corrected or discredited, or reliable contemporaneous evidence establishes that the supposed government reluctance did not exist.
